description: Obtain information about a specific versions of DB engines.

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: db_parameter_group_family
parameters.description: The name of a specific RDS parameter group family to return details for.

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: default_only
parameters.description: Specifies whether to return only the default version of the specified engine or the engine and major version combination. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: The database engine to return version details for. Choices: "aurora-mysql" "aurora-postgresql" "custom-oracle-ee" "db2-ae" "db2-se" "mariadb" "mysql" "oracle-ee" "oracle-ee-cdb" "oracle-se2" "oracle-se2-cdb" "postgres" "sqlserver-ee" "sqlserver-se" "sqlserver-ex" "sqlserver-web"

parameters.name: engine_version
parameters.description: A specific database engine version to return details for.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: A filter that specifies one or more DB engine versions to describe. See https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/APIReference/API_DescribeDBEngineVersions.html.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

examples:
- name: List all of the available parameter group families for the Aurora PostgreSQL DB engine
  amazon.aws.rds_engine_versions_info:
    engine: aurora-postgresql

- name: List all of the available parameter group families for the Aurora PostgreSQL DB engine on a specific version
  amazon.aws.rds_engine_versions_info:
    engine: aurora-postgresql
    engine_version: 16.1

- name: Get default engine version for DB parameter group family postgres16
  amazon.aws.rds_engine_versions_info:
    engine: postgres
    default_only: true
    db_parameter_group_family: postgres16

return_values.name: db_engine_versions
return_values.description: List of RDS engine versions. Returned: always

return_values.name: create_time
return_values.description: The creation time of the DB engine version. Returned: success

return_values.name: custom_db_engine_version_manifest
return_values.description: JSON string that lists the installation files and parameters that RDS Custom uses to create a custom engine version (CEV). Returned: success

return_values.name: database_installation_files_s3_bucket_name
return_values.description: The name of the Amazon S3 bucket that contains your database installation files. Returned: success

return_values.name: database_installation_files_s3_prefix
return_values.description: The Amazon S3 directory that contains the database installation files. Returned: success

return_values.name: db_engine_description
return_values.description: The description of the database engine. Returned: success

return_values.name: db_engine_media_type
return_values.description: A value that indicates the source media provider of the AMI based on the usage operation. Returned: success

return_values.name: db_engine_version_arn
return_values.description: The ARN of the custom engine version. Returned: success

return_values.name: db_engine_version_description
return_values.description: The description of the database engine version. Returned: success

return_values.name: db_parameter_group_family
return_values.description: The name of the DB parameter group family for the database engine. Returned: success

return_values.name: default_character_set
return_values.description: The default character set for new instances of this engine version. Returned: success Sample: {"character_set_description": "Unicode 5.0 UTF-8 Universal character set", "character_set_name": "AL32UTF8"}

return_values.name: engine
return_values.description: The name of the database engine. Returned: success

return_values.name: engine_version
return_values.description: The version number of the database engine. Returned: success

return_values.name: exportable_log_types
return_values.description: The types of logs that the database engine has available for export to CloudWatch Logs. Returned: success

return_values.name: image
return_values.description: The EC2 image Returned: success

return_values.name: image_id
return_values.description: A value that indicates the ID of the AMI. Returned: success

return_values.name: status
return_values.description: A value that indicates the status of a custom engine version (CEV). Returned: success

return_values.name: kms_key_id
return_values.description: The Amazon Web Services KMS key identifier for an encrypted CEV. Returned: success

return_values.name: major_engine_version
return_values.description: The major engine version of the CEV. Returned: success

return_values.name: supported_ca_certificate_identifiers
return_values.description: A list of the supported CA certificate identifiers. Returned: success Sample: ["rds-ca-2019", "rds-ca-ecc384-g1", "rds-ca-rsa4096-g1", "rds-ca-rsa2048-g1"]

return_values.name: supported_character_sets
return_values.description: A list of the character sets supported by this engine for the CharacterSetName parameter of the CreateDBInstance operation. Returned: success

return_values.name: character_set_description
return_values.description: The description of the character set. Returned: success

return_values.name: character_set_name
return_values.description: The name of the character set. Returned: success

return_values.name: supported_engine_modes
return_values.description: A list of the supported DB engine modes. Returned: success

return_values.name: supported_feature_names
return_values.description: A list of features supported by the DB engine. Returned: success Sample: ["Comprehend", "Lambda", "s3Export", "s3Import", "SageMaker"]

return_values.name: supported_nchar_character_sets
return_values.description: A list of the character sets supported by the Oracle DB engine. Returned: success

return_values.name: supported_timezones
return_values.description: A list of the time zones supported by this engine for the Timezone parameter of the CreateDBInstance action. Returned: success Sample: [{"TimezoneName": "xxx"}]

return_values.name: supports_babelfish
return_values.description: Indicates whether the engine version supports Babelfish for Aurora PostgreSQL. Returned: success

return_values.name: supports_certificate_rotation_without_restart
return_values.description: Indicates whether the engine version supports rotating the server certificate without rebooting the DB instance. Returned: success

return_values.name: supports_global_databases
return_values.description: Indicates whether you can use Aurora global databases with a specific DB engine version. Returned: success

return_values.name: supports_integrations
return_values.description: Indicates whether the DB engine version supports zero-ETL integrations with Amazon Redshift. Returned: success

return_values.name: supports_local_write_forwarding
return_values.description: Indicates whether the DB engine version supports forwarding write operations from reader DB instances to the writer DB instance in the DB cluster. Returned: success

return_values.name: supports_log_exports_to_cloudwatchLogs
return_values.description: Indicates whether the engine version supports exporting the log types specified by ExportableLogTypes to CloudWatch Logs. Returned: success

return_values.name: supports_parallel_query
return_values.description: Indicates whether you can use Aurora parallel query with a specific DB engine version. Returned: success

return_values.name: supports_read_replica
return_values.description: Indicates whether the database engine version supports read replicas. Returned: success

return_values.name: tags
return_values.description: A dictionary of key value pairs. Returned: success Sample: {"some": "tag"}

return_values.name: valid_upgrade_target
return_values.description: A list of engine versions that this database engine version can be upgraded to. Returned: success Sample: [{"auto_upgrade": false, "description": "Aurora PostgreSQL (Compatible with PostgreSQL 15.5)", "engine": "aurora-postgresql", "engine_version": "15.5", "is_major_version_upgrade": false, "supported_engine_modes": ["provisioned"], "supports_babelfish": true, "supports_global_databases": true, "supports_integrations": false, "supports_local_write_forwarding": true, "supports_parallel_query": false}]
